answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may accept paid work, with the stake slashed if peers attest fraud. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, so an attacker must fund a whole ridge of deposits rather than one cheap knoll of sock puppets. Honest work slowly earns the stake back, while a single ember of proven fraud burns the deposit and the reputation attached to it.
